mainTopic: Liability for words alone after being incited to idol worship, and whether worshipping out of love or fear makes one liable
overview: This amud opens at the end of an answer to a contradiction between two משניות. One משנה makes a person liable just for saying 'I will worship' an idol. The other suggests that saying 'yes' to a מסית is not enough. First the גמרא finishes an earlier point: when someone asks people to worship him, their 'yes' is only mockery. Then, turning to the משניות, one answer splits the cases into an incited individual and an incited crowd, and רב יוסף supports it with a פסוק. אביי knocks this answer out with a ברייתא showing that the two cases differ only in body and property. אביי, רבא, רב אשי and רבינא then each give their own resolution. Next comes a new מחלוקת: אביי says someone who worships out of love or fear of a person is חייב, while רבא says he is פטור unless he accepted the idol as a god. אביי brings proofs from a משנה and from the ברייתא about המן, and רבא deflects both. אביי then begins a proof from a כהן משיח who sinned by mistake with עבודה זרה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 'yes' was only mockery
steps.stepSummary: The earlier answer finishes: the incited people answer 'yes' only to make fun of the מסית, so they are not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They think: what makes him different from us? So when they say 'yes,' they are really just laughing at him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from before this section. It explains why people who answer 'yes' to someone asking them to worship him are not liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one asking to be worshipped is a person no different from them, so nobody takes the offer seriously. Their 'yes' is sarcasm, not real acceptance of an idol. So their 'yes' does not make them liable.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Yes
Mocking, laughing at

phrases.english: What is different about him
from us ourselves?
phrases.notes: The listeners think to themselves: why worship someone no different from us?

phrases.english: And the 'yes' that they say,
is mocking him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא אִיהוּ מִינַּן דִּידַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the 'yes' is not real agreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'yes' to a מסית should make the incited person liable, just like saying 'I will worship.'
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the 'yes' is mockery, so it is not acceptance of idol worship.

steps.title: Individual versus crowd
steps.stepSummary: A way to settle the two משניות: one is about an individual who was incited, the other about a crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משניות can be explained this way: one is about a single person who was incited, the other about many people who were incited. A single person does not stop to reconsider, so he goes astray after the idol. A crowd talks it over and reconsiders, so they do not go astray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the contradiction between the two משניות. The split is by how many people were incited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one person says 'yes,' he really means it, so his words alone make him liable. A crowd tends to discuss and change its mind, so their 'yes' is not a final decision and does not make them liable. Each משנה is now about a different situation.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual who was incited
A crowd that was incited
Reconsiders, changes his mind
Goes astray after it

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same words ('yes, I will worship') can carry different weight depending on who says them and how seriously they are meant.

phrases.english: And the משניות: here, with an individual who was incited,
there, with a crowd who were incited.
An individual does not reconsider,
and he goes astray after it;
a crowd reconsiders,
and they do not go astray after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַתְנְיָתִין: כָּאן בְּיָחִיד הַנִּיסָּת, כָּאן בְּרַבִּים הַנִּיסָּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns (ומתניתין) from step 1's point to the contradiction between the two משניות and answers it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: individual versus crowd.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to describe the same kind of 'yes' and should give the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: An individual who says 'yes' is liable; a crowd that says 'yes' is not, because a crowd reconsiders.

steps.title: A פסוק supports the individual being liable
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a פסוק showing that agreeing to and listening to the מסית makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: How do I know this? Because it is written, 'You shall not approve of him, nor listen to him.' That means if he did approve and listen, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף supports the answer in step 2 with a פסוק. He shows the תורה treats agreeing with the מסית as something you can be liable for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids approving and listening, which implies that someone who does approve and listen is liable, even without actually worshipping. The פסוק speaks to one person ('you'), which fits the individual case from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this?
Approve, agree
Liable

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
From where do I say it?
As it is written: 'You shall not approve of him,
nor listen to him.'
This implies: if he approved and listened, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the individual-versus-crowd answer.
steps.raayaObject: That an individual who agrees to the מסית is liable for agreeing alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:9, 'לֹא תֹאבֶה לוֹ וְלֹא תִשְׁמַע אֵלָיו.'

steps.title: אביי: individual and crowd are one category
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא saying the פסוק of מסית includes both an individual and a crowd.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: Is there really a difference between a crowd that was incited and an individual who was incited? But a ברייתא teaches on the פסוק 'If your brother, the son of your mother, incites you': both an individual who was incited and a crowd who were incited are included. The תורה then took the individual out of the crowd's group, and the crowd out of the individual's group.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the answer from step 2. He brings a ברייתא showing that the פסוק covers both individual and crowd together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the individual and the crowd are treated differently when they say 'yes.' The ברייתא says both start in the same category under the same פסוק. Only specific points were separated out by the תורה, so why invent a new difference that the תורה did not single out?

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to him (from a teaching)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Incites you
The פסוק took out (separated)
From the category of

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying individual and crowd are identical in every rule. The ברייתא itself admits the תורה separated them on certain points; his point is that they share one basic category.

phrases.english: Abaye objected to him:
Is there a difference between an incited crowd
and an incited individual?
But isn't it taught:
'If your brother, the son of your mother, incites you'
both an individual who was incited
and a crowd who were incited are included,
and the פסוק took the individual out of the crowd's category
and the crowd out of the individual's category.
phrases.notes: Meaning: they start as one group, and a separate פסוק gives each its own special rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִי שָׁאנֵי בֵּין נִיסָּת דְּרַבִּים לְנִיסָּת יָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the individual-versus-crowd distinction that רב יוסף supported in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that an incited individual and an incited crowd are treated differently.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא puts both in the same category under one פסוק, with only specific differences singled out by the תורה, so a new difference based on 'reconsidering' seems unfounded.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists how a single person and a crowd are treated differently
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that אביי quoted continues. A single incited person is treated more strictly for his body and more leniently for his property. An incited crowd is the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A single person was taken out of the crowd's category to be stricter with his body and more lenient with his property. The crowd was taken out of the single person's category to be more lenient with their bodies and stricter with their property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the words of the ברייתא that אביי brought against רב יוסף. This is the evidence; the punchline comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה wrote the case of a single incited person and the case of a whole city separately for a reason. Each case is taken out of the other's rule to give it a different punishment for the body and a different result for property. That tells us exactly where the two cases differ.

keyTerms.meaning: A single individual who was incited to worship idols
A multitude, meaning an entire city that was led astray (עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת)
From the category of; singled out from a general rule
His body, meaning the type of death penalty
His property, meaning whether his belongings are destroyed

steps.confusionAlert: Being "stricter" for the single person does not mean the crowd goes unpunished. Both are put to death. The difference is only in the type of death and in what happens to the property.

phrases.english: An individual was taken out of the category of the multitude,
to be stricter with his body
phrases.notes: A single person gets stoning (סקילה), while the people of an עיר הנדחת get the sword (סייף).

phrases.english: and more lenient with his property.
The multitude was taken out of the category of the individual,
to be more lenient with their bodies
and stricter with their property.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָחִיד מִכְּלַל רַבִּים, לְהַחְמִיר עַל גּוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the text of the ברייתא that אביי began quoting in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The יחיד/רבים distinction used to settle the two משניות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא spells out the specific ways a single person and a crowd differ, which sets up the inference that they differ in nothing else.

steps.title: They differ only in these matters and are the same in everything else
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from the ברייתא that a single person and a crowd differ only in body and property. In every other matter, including liability for just saying "I will worship," they are the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: Only in this matter are they different. In every other matter they are like each other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws the conclusion from the ברייתא. Since it lists only body and property as differences, the single-person versus crowd split cannot explain the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 2, backed by רב יוסף's פסוק in step 3, claimed that a single person and a crowd differ about whether speech alone makes one liable. The ברייתא shows the תורה separated them only for body and property. So there is no room for a further difference about speech, and that answer falls.

keyTerms.meaning: In this matter
It is different
They are like one another; they are the same

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: when a source lists specific differences, we infer that there are no other differences. Here it knocks out the earlier answer.

phrases.english: It is in this matter that they are different,
but in all other matters
they are like each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא מִילְּתָא הוּא דְּשָׁאנֵי, אֲבָל בְּכֹל מִילֵּי כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא just quoted and completes אביי's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that one משנה is about a single person and the other is about a crowd (step 2), supported by רב יוסף (step 3)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only body and property as differences. That implies the two cases are the same about liability for speech, so the משניות cannot be split along those lines.

steps.title: אביי's answer: deciding on your own versus being talked into it
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new way to settle the two משניות. One is about a person who decided to worship on his own; he may still change his mind, so speech alone does not make him liable. The other is about a person who was talked into it by others; he gets dragged after them, so his saying "yes" makes him liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Here it is about someone who was persuaded by himself. There it is about someone persuaded by others. A person who decides on his own will think it over again. A person persuaded by others gets pulled along after them.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked out the earlier answer, אביי offers his own way to explain why one משנה makes a person liable for words and the other does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is no longer how many people were involved. It is where the idea came from. Someone who talks himself into it has not really committed, because he is likely to reconsider. Someone pushed by others is likely to follow through, so his verbal agreement already counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and offers a new one
Is persuaded or incited
By himself, on his own initiative
He reconsiders; he is likely to change his mind
He is dragged after them

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's final split: a person who decides on his own is not liable for just saying "I will worship" because he may back down. A person talked into it by others is liable for saying it because he follows them.

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said:
Here, it is about one who is persuaded by himself,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה that makes a person liable only for actually worshipping.

phrases.english: there, it is about one who is persuaded by others.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה that makes a person liable for just saying "I will go and worship."

phrases.english: By himself, he thinks it over again,
by others, he is dragged after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כָּאן – בְּנִיסָּת מִפִּי עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the יחיד/רבים answer in step 6, אביי gives a new way to settle the two משניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two משניות are about different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the difference between the משניות was a single person versus a crowd.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is whether the person decided on his own, so he may reconsider, or was persuaded by others, so he follows them.

steps.title: אביי brings a verse to back up his distinction
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his distinction from the פסוק "לא תאבה לו ולא תשמע אליו." It shows that a person talked into it by a מסית is liable once he agrees and listens.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? The פסוק says: "Do not agree with him, and do not listen to him." So if he did agree and listen, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows where in the תורה his distinction (from step 7) comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is talking about someone a מסית is trying to talk into idol worship. It warns him not to agree or listen, so agreeing is itself the sin. That fits אביי's rule that a person pulled along by others is liable just for saying "yes."

keyTerms.meaning: How do I know this? (an opening for bringing a proof)
Do not agree with him (the מסית)
He agreed and listened

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק רב יוסף used back in step 3. אביי is not repeating him by mistake. He now uses the פסוק to support his own distinction: it speaks about someone pushed by others.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say this?
As it is written: "You shall not agree with him
and you shall not listen to him."
This implies: if he agreed and listened, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a Torah source for the distinction אביי made in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that a person talked into it by others is liable just for agreeing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:9, לא תאבה לו ולא תשמע אליו, which speaks about a person being pushed by a מסית.

steps.title: רבא's different way to settle the two משניות
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both משניות are about a person talked into it by others. One is a case where the מסית described the idol's powers, and the other is a case where he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Both משניות are about someone talked into it by others. One is where the מסית told him, "This is how it eats, this is how it drinks, this is how it does good, this is how it does harm." The other is where the מסית did not tell him all that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different way to settle the contradiction between the two משניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי divided the cases by who started it: the person himself, or others. רבא says both cases are about a person pushed by others. The real difference is whether the מסית convinced him by describing the idol's powers. If he heard that and said "yes," he really means it, so he is liable for speech alone. Without that description, his "yes" is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one
Talked into it by other people
This is how it eats (describing the idol)
It does good / it does harm

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two approaches. For אביי, the question is who started it. For רבא, both cases have a מסית, and the question is whether he described the idol's powers.

phrases.english: Rava says:
Both this and that are about one talked into it by others,
this one is where he said to him:
"This is how it eats," "this is how it drinks,"
"this is how it does good," "this is how it does harm,"
and that one is where he did not say to him:
"This is how it eats," "this is how it drinks," and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּנִיסָּת מִפִּי אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different resolution from אביי's in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): both are a case of a מסית, split by whether the idol's powers were described.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the split must be between a person who started on his own and a person pushed by others (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are about a person pushed by others. He is liable for agreeing in words only if the מסית convinced him with a description of the idol's powers.

steps.title: רבא's verse: from the gods nearby you learn about the gods far away
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the פסוק about the gods of the peoples "near" and "far." He explains that the near gods, which you can see are worthless, teach you that the far ones are worthless too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? The פסוק says: "From the gods of the peoples around you, those near you" and so on. Why should it matter whether they are near or far? The תורה is telling you this: from what the near gods are like, you can learn what the far gods are like.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a פסוק to support his distinction, and first explains what the פסוק is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems strange for the תורה to mention distance, since idol worship is forbidden either way. רבא explains that the תורה is giving you a way to answer the מסית. The idols near you clearly have no power, so any idol far away that he praises has no power either. This step lays the groundwork; the next step draws the proof from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Near ones / far ones
What difference does it make to me?
This is what it is telling you
Their nature, what they are really like

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As it is written: "From the gods of the peoples
that are around you, those near to you, etc."

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי קְרוֹבִים וּמָה לִי רְחוֹקִים?
phrases.english: What difference is it to me if they are near, and what if they are far?
This is what it is telling you:
From the nature of the near ones you learn
what the nature of the far ones is.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the Torah support for רבא's distinction from step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that being liable for speech depends on the idol's powers being described.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:8, הקרבים אליך או הרחקים ממך, read as telling you to judge the far gods by the near ones.

steps.title: The verse must be about a מסית who praised the idol's powers
steps.stepSummary: The verse speaks of a מסית describing the idol's powers. So that is the case where agreeing makes a person liable, which proves רבא's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the פסוק talking about a case where the מסית said, "This is how it eats, this is how it drinks, this is how it does good, this is how it does harm"? Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof: the פסוק assumes the מסית described the idol's powers, and that confirms his distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah only needs to say "judge the far gods by the near ones" if the מסית is praising some faraway idol's powers. So the פסוק pictures a מסית who describes how the idol eats, drinks, helps, and harms. That is the convincing kind of מסית, where saying "yes" already makes a person liable, just as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (pointing to the obvious reading)
Learn from it: the proof stands

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: both משניות are about a person pushed by a מסית. If the מסית described the idol's powers ("this is how it eats, drinks, does good, does harm"), agreeing in words makes the person liable. If not, it does not. His source is the פסוק about gods "near" and "far."

phrases.english: Is it not where he said to him:
"This is how it eats, this is how it drinks,
this is how it does good, this is how it does harm"?
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the proof from the reading of the פסוק given in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק is about a convincing מסית who praised the idol's powers, which proves רבא's distinction.

steps.title: רב אשי: the later משנה is about an apostate
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי settles the contradiction by saying the סיפא, which makes a person liable for speech alone, is talking about a ישראל משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the later clause is talking about a Jew who has already left the faith.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers another way to settle the two משניות. He says the one that makes a person liable just for saying 'I will worship' is about a ישראל משומד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who has already turned away from Judaism means it when he says he will worship, so his words count as final and he is liable. A regular Jew might still change his mind, so speech alone does not make him liable. This is a different split from אביי's (decided alone vs. talked into it) and רבא's (powers described vs. not).

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause (here, the later משנה that makes speech liable)
A Jew who has turned away from the faith

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The latter clause is about an apostate Jew.
phrases.notes: The סיפא here is the משנה that makes someone liable just for saying 'I will worship.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: סֵיפָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּמָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative answer to the same contradiction, alongside the approaches of אביי and רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the type of person (משומד vs. regular Jew).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to describe the same kind of person, so they seem to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Speech makes a ישראל משומד liable, but not a regular Jew.

steps.title: רבינא: the משנה teaches 'not only this, but also that'
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says there is no contradiction at all. The משנה is teaching in a 'לא זו אף זו' style, from the simpler law to the bigger חידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the תנא is teaching 'not only this, but even this.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives the last answer to the contradiction. He says the משנה is simply teaching step by step, from an easier rule to a harder one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the משנה teaches the obvious rule that someone who actually worships is liable. Then it adds a bigger חידוש: even someone who only says he will worship is liable. So the two rules do not clash. The second one just goes further than the first.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches 'not only this, but even this,' building from the simple case to the bigger חידוש

steps.confusionAlert: In a 'לא זו אף זו' list, the later item is the bigger חידוש. The earlier item is not the limit of the law.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It teaches: not only this, but also that.

steps.whatToRemember: After the יחיד/רבים answer is rejected (step 6), these answers to the contradiction still stand: the mockery answer (step 1), אביי (decided alone vs. talked into it), רבא (powers described vs. not), רב אשי (משומד), and רבינא (לא זו אף זו).
steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: לָא זוֹ אַף זוֹ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative answer that ends the discussion of the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה's style as a 'לא זו אף זו' list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to make speech not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה adds that even speech makes a person liable, as a bigger חידוש.

steps.title: Worshipping out of love or fear: אביי says liable, רבא says exempt
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: if someone worships an idol only out of love or fear of a person, אביי holds he is חייב and רבא holds he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: someone who worships an idol out of love or out of fear. אביי says he is liable. רבא says he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת between אביי and רבא. It is about someone who worships an idol only because he loves or fears a person, not because he believes in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the physical act of worship is enough, or whether the person must also believe in the idol. Here both sides only state their rulings. Their reasons come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a מחלוקת of the אמוראים)
Out of love (for a person who asked him to bow)
Out of fear (of a person forcing him)
Liable / exempt

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who worships an idol
out of love or out of fear,
phrases.notes: Love or fear of a person, not of the idol. He doesn't actually believe in it.

phrases.english: Abaye says: he is liable;
Rava says: he is exempt.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about worshipping out of love or fear of the idol. It is about love or fear of a human being.
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מֵאַהֲבָה וּמִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the contradiction behind and starts a new מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: someone who worships out of love or fear is liable. רבא: he is exempt.

steps.title: The reasons: the act itself versus accepting it as a god
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he is חייב because he did the act of worship. רבא says he is פטור, because liability depends on accepting the idol as a god.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says he is liable, because he did worship it. רבא says he is exempt: if he accepted it upon himself as a god, yes, he is liable. If not, he is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reasoning behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the act decides: he worshipped, so he is liable, whatever his reason. For רבא, the heart decides: there is only liability if he truly accepted the idol as a god. Love or fear of a person does not mean he did that.

keyTerms.meaning: Because he did worship it
He accepted it upon himself as a god
Yes / no

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the סוגיא that follows: does עבודה זרה need real acceptance of the idol, or is the act enough?

phrases.english: Abaye says: he is liable,
because he worshipped it.
Rava says: he is exempt,
if he accepted it upon himself as a god, yes;
if not, no.

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: the act of worship alone makes him liable. רבא: only real acceptance of the idol as a god makes him liable.
steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אֲמַר: חַיָּיב, דְּהָא פַּלְחַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the rulings stated in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the act of worship is enough. רבא: liability needs real acceptance of the idol as a god.

steps.title: A memory sign for אביי's proofs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a short memory sign to help remember the order of אביי's proofs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory sign: 'A slave will bow to the anointed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next part of the discussion. Before listing אביי's proofs, it gives a short phrase to help us remember them in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the סימן points to one of the proofs that follow. 'עֶבֶד' points to the משנה's word 'הָעוֹבֵד', and 'יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה' points to the ברייתא about bowing. This line is not an argument; it just organizes what comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign; a short phrase that helps you remember a list of teachings in order
A slave; here it hints at the word 'הָעוֹבֵד' (one who worships)
Will bow; here it hints at the פסוק 'לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה'

steps.confusionAlert: The סימן is not a real statement about slaves or a משיח. It is only a memory device made of hint-words.

phrases.english: Memory sign:
A slave will bow to the anointed.
phrases.notes: Each word hints at one of אביי's proofs: 'slave' for 'one who worships,' 'bow' for the ברייתא, and 'anointed' for a proof that comes later.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: עֶבֶד יִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לְמָשִׁיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the list of proofs that אביי will bring for his position from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; this is a memory sign for the proofs that follow.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the repeated word in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the משנה's extra phrase 'אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵד' comes to include someone who worships out of love or fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view? From the משנה: 'One who worships an idol... this includes one who worships...' Doesn't the extra 'one who worships' come to include someone who worships out of love or fear?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his first proof that worshipping out of love or fear makes a person חייב. He points to a משנה that seems to say 'one who worships' twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said 'הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה', so saying 'אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵד' again looks extra. אביי suggests the extra phrase adds a new case: someone who worships without believing in the idol, only out of love or fear. If that is right, such a person is חייב, just like אביי said.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? An opening for bringing a proof for one's own view
As we learned (in a משנה)
Is it not...? A way of suggesting how a source should be read
Out of love or out of fear (of a person, not out of belief in the idol)

phrases.english: And Abaye said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: How do I know that someone who worships out of love or fear is חייב?

phrases.english: As we learned: One who worships idols,
this includes one who worships, etc.
Is it not
to include one who worships out of love or out of fear?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof from a משנה for אביי's view in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that worshipping out of love or fear makes a person חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's seemingly extra phrase 'אֶחָד הָעוֹבֵד', which אביי reads as adding the case of worship out of love or fear.

steps.title: רבא reads the משנה like רבי ירמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof: the extra 'הָעוֹבֵד' is explained the way רבי ירמיה already explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא would answer you: No, the phrase means what רבי ירמיה explained.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's proof. He says the extra word in the משנה has a different job, as רבי ירמיה already explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof only works if the extra phrase must be about love or fear. רבא shows there is another reading: רבי ירמיה used it to separate two cases. Worshipping in the idol's usual way is one case, and offering a sacrifice makes you חייב even if that is not the idol's usual way. Since the extra phrase already has a use, it proves nothing about love or fear.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבא would say to you; the גמרא shows how the other side would answer
As (he) explains or answers it
An אמורא who explained this משנה earlier

phrases.english: And Rava would say to you: No,
it is as Rabbi Yirmeya explains.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר לָךְ: לָא, כְּדִמְתָרֵץ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof from the משנה in Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not אביי's overall position.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra phrase 'הָעוֹבֵד' already has another explanation (רבי ירמיה's), so it does not have to refer to worship out of love or fear.

steps.title: אביי's proof from bowing to המן
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: you may bow to a person, but not to someone worshipped like a god, like המן. Since people worshipped המן out of fear, worship out of fear is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view? From a ברייתא: 'You shall not bow to them.' To them (idols) you may not bow, but you may bow to a person like yourself. Could it be that you may bow even to a person who is worshipped, like המן? So the פסוק says: 'Nor worship them.' And people worshipped המן only out of fear!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second proof, this time from a ברייתא about bowing to people. He points out that the ברייתא forbids worshipping a person like המן, and people only worshipped המן out of fear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows bowing to an ordinary person as a sign of respect, but it forbids bowing to someone who is treated as a god, like המן. Nobody truly believed המן was a god; they bowed because they were afraid of him. So אביי argues that the ברייתא forbids worship done only out of fear, which supports his view that such a person is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
To a person like yourself; bowing to an ordinary person as respect
Worshipped; a person treated like a god
The פסוק teaches; introduces the verse that answers the 'I might have thought'
But isn't it so that...; introduces the key point of the proof

steps.whyThisMatters: This proof moves from reading a משנה to a real case. המן is a clear example of worship done from fear, not belief, so it seems to fit אביי's view directly.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?
As it was taught: "You shall not bow to them" –
to them you may not bow,
but you may bow to a person like yourself.
I might think even one who is worshipped, like Haman?
The verse teaches: "Nor worship them."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: But Haman was worshipped out of fear!
phrases.notes: This is אביי talking now, not the ברייתא. He is pointing out why it proves his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא rejected the first proof in Step 18, אביי brings a new proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that worship done only out of fear (or love) is still forbidden and makes a person חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'לֹא תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה לָהֶם... וְלֹא תָעׇבְדֵם', which forbids bowing to someone worshipped like המן, whom people worshipped out of fear.

steps.title: רבא explains the Haman case differently
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא compares the case to המן only in one way: המן was treated as an idol. It does not compare them in the fear part, so it proves nothing about worship out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא says: like המן, but not like המן. Like המן, in that he himself was treated as an idol. Not like המן, because people bowed to המן out of fear, while here the case is not out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's proof from המן. He says the ברייתא only borrows one feature of המן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי read 'like המן' as covering everything about המן, including that people feared him. רבא splits the comparison. It is 'like המן' because the person is treated as a god, but 'not like המן' because the ברייתא means someone who bows without fear. So the ברייתא forbids real belief-worship, and fear-worship stays פטור, which fits רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like המן, and not like המן: similar in one way only
He himself
Out of fear
And here (in our case)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא denies that המן was worshipped. He agrees המן was treated as an idol. He only says that people bowed to המן out of fear, and that fear part is not what the ברייתא is talking about.

phrases.english: And Rava [explains]: like Haman, and not like Haman.
Like Haman, in that he himself was [treated as] an idol;
and not like Haman, since Haman [was bowed to] out of fear,
while here it is not out of fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא: כְּהָמָן וְלֹא כְּהָמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the המן ברייתא only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed the comparison to המן includes the fear part. רבא says it only includes המן being treated as a god.

steps.title: אביי brings a new source about the anointed priest
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא about a כהן משיח who serves עבודה זרה by mistake. רבי says he brings a קרבן for a mistaken act. The חכמים say he brings one only if he did not know the הלכה. Both sides agree on two details.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: From where do I say this? As it was taught: a כהן משיח who sinned with עבודה זרה. רבי says he brings a קרבן for a mistaken act. The חכמים say only for not knowing the law. They agree that he brings a female goat like a regular person. They also agree that he does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new proof for his view by quoting a ברייתא. This step only lays out the source; the reasoning comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן גדול brings a קרבן only when he did not know the הלכה itself. רבי says that for עבודה זרה he also brings one for a mistaken act. אביי will focus on what such a 'mistaken act' could be. The two points both sides agree on are part of the quote but are not the core of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (an opening for a proof)
The anointed priest, the כהן גדול
A mistake in the act itself
Not knowing the הלכה itself
A female goat brought as a חטאת
A guilt-offering brought when unsure whether one sinned

phrases.english: And Abaye said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught: an anointed priest [who sinned] with idol worship,
Rabbi says: [he brings an offering] for a mistaken act,
and the Rabbis say: [only] for a lack of knowing the law.
And they agree that [he brings] a female goat, like an individual.
And they agree that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא rejected the המן proof, אביי turns to a different source.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that worshipping out of love or fear makes one חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי's view that a כהן משיח brings a קרבן for a mistaken act of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: What could a mistaken act of idol worship be?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what case רבי means. He rules out a priest who bowed to a building he thought was a בית הכנסת, because his heart was toward Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: This mistaken act of עבודה זרה, what does it look like? If he thought it was a בית הכנסת and bowed to it, his heart was toward Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks what situation רבי's 'mistaken act' refers to. He rejects the first possible case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mistaken act means he knew the הלכה but erred about the facts. The obvious case is bowing to a building he thought was a בית הכנסת. But that person meant to serve ה׳, so it is not even a sin needing a קרבן. אביי needs another case.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances?
He thought
Behold, his heart is toward Heaven

phrases.english: This mistaken act of idol worship,
phrases.notes: This is רבי's case from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: what are its circumstances?
If he thought it was a synagogue
and bowed to it,
his heart is toward Heaven!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי שִׁגְגַת מַעֲשֶׂה דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, הֵיכִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes רבי's view from the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real case counts as a mistaken act of עבודה זרה according to רבי.

steps.title: The case is bowing to a statue of a person
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that the mistaken act must be a case where the priest saw a statue of a person and bowed to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is where he saw a statue and bowed to it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers his own question: the case is bowing to a statue. This sets up the next part of his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing to a statue of a person is a real act toward something that is worshipped. אביי will next ask why this counts only as a mistake. That question leads toward bowing out of love or fear, which supports his view.

keyTerms.meaning: A statue (usually of a king or person)
And he bowed to it

phrases.english: Rather, where he saw a statue
and bowed to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דַּחֲזָא אִנְדְּרָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistaken act is bowing to a statue of a person.

steps.title: Accepting the statue as a god would be on purpose, not a mistake
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules out one version of the statue case: if the priest accepted the statue as a god, he is a מזיד and not a שוגג, so he would not bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he accepted it upon himself as a god, he is an intentional sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tests the case he just proposed, a priest bowing to a statue of a person, and rejects one way of reading it. This narrows the case. The explanation of what the priest was thinking continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן is brought only for a mistake, which is called שוגג. If the priest bowed to the statue while really accepting it as his god, he knew what he was doing. That makes him a מזיד, who gets punished and does not bring a קרבן. So רבי's mistaken act must be a case where the priest did not accept the statue as a god.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it upon himself as a god, meaning he truly treated it as his deity.
Someone who sins on purpose. He is punished and cannot fix the sin with a קרבן.
Someone who sins by mistake. This is the person who brings a קרבן.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is dropping the statue case. He keeps it, but says the priest must have bowed without accepting the statue as a god. Only that version can count as a mistake.

phrases.english: If he accepted it upon himself as a god
phrases.notes: "It" is the statue of a person from the previous step, the one the priest bowed to.

phrases.english: he is an intentional sinner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַבְּלֵיהּ עֲלֵיהּ בֶּאֱלוֹהַּ מֵזִיד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the case from step 23 (bowing to a statue of a person) and rules out the version where the priest accepted it as a god.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only one version of the statue case, where the priest accepts the statue as a god. The statue case itself stays.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Accepting the statue as a god is a deliberate act of עבודה זרה (מזיד), and a קרבן is only brought for a mistake (שוגג).
